purpose: Machine-readable transcription of the corrected CIC-IDS2017 labelling rules (Liu, Engelen et al., IEEE CNS 2022) in the EXP93 CorrectedRuleSet rule format for a raw-PCAP evaluation of the 2017 captures.
timezone_note: CIC-IDS2017 was captured in Fredericton, Canada (Atlantic Daylight Time, UTC-3) on 2017-07-03..07. The corrected CICFlowMeter outputs timestamps in UTC and the notebook states 'Timestamps are in NANOSECONDS (!) Unix time. Note that the CSV files are in the UTC timezone.' Every start_ns/end_ns below is copied verbatim from the notebook (UTC epoch ns); each rule's window_note prints the UTC wall clock and the derived ADT wall clock for checking against the original CIC schedule (e.g. FTP-Patator 12:17 UTC = 09:17 ADT, CIC lists 9:20-10:20). No local-time string was converted; the notebook never gives local times.
label_rule_note: Rules transcribe the notebook's label_flows calls (time window, src/dst IPs and ports, payload_filter and additional_filters). Later notebook calls overwrite earlier labels, so each later call is given a higher 'priority' (CorrectedRuleSet sorts by -priority then id; attempted rules carry no 'label' so they never cause a label conflict). Differences from the notebook that the matcher imposes: (1) the notebook tests the CICFlowMeter flow-start Timestamp against the window, whereas CorrectedRuleSet requires the whole session inside the window and marks partial overlaps 'boundary'; (2) the notebook matches Src IP/Dst IP directionally, CorrectedRuleSet matches bidirectionally with the rule source as the 'attack' side, so victim-frame notebook rules are restated in the attacker frame; (3) the notebook's 'Total Length of Fwd Packet' == attack payload bytes, 'Total Fwd Packet' == attack packets, 'Flow Duration' (us) == flow_duration; (4) no protocol condition is added because the notebook has none. Conditions the matcher cannot express are kept in 'todo_condition' with 'status': 'requires_matcher_extension' and proposed field names (max_peer_payload_bytes, min_peer_packets, max_peer_packets); the matcher ignores unknown fields, so read the per-rule consequence before running.

matcher_extensions_required.meaning: upper bound on payload bytes sent by the peer (victim) side
upper bound on packets sent by the peer side
lower bound on packets sent by the peer side

matcher_extensions_required.field: (new) exclude flows by Fwd Packet Length Max == 408 or attack payload in {176, 20514}
matcher_extensions_required.meaning: per-destination exclusion of benign background; no existing field; rule over-labels until implemented

pcap_source_note: Original PCAPs are distributed by the Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity (https://www.unb.ca/cic/datasets/ids-2017.html) as one file per day (Monday..Friday-WorkingHours.pcap); the authors ran pcapfix then reordercap before CICFlowMeter. No download url/member fields are given here because the EXP93 fetch step expects zip members and the 2017 files are plain PCAPs; add them after verifying the mirror.

family_mapping_note: Proposed families: bf (FTP/SSH-Patator), dos (Slowloris, Slowhttptest, Hulk, GoldenEye), heartbleed, web (Brute Force, XSS, SQL Injection), inf (Infiltration Communication and Cool disk - MAC), bot (Ares), portscan (Friday Portscan AND Thursday 'Infiltration - Portscan'), ddos (LOIC HTTP). Decision to confirm: the notebook's separate label 'Infiltration - Portscan' is mapped to portscan because it is behaviourally a port scan (rounds 2-3 originate from the compromised host 192.168.10.8); the original CIC dataset labelled those flows Infiltration, so 'inf' is the alternative. Every '*-Attempted-*' annotation maps to benign, which is what CorrectedRuleSet does at runtime via unmatched_policy; attempted_categories lists the parent family if merging is preferred.

known_issues: Timestamps: the corrected CICFlowMeter writes UTC with microsecond precision and the notebook windows are UTC Unix nanoseconds ('Note that the CSV files are in the UTC timezone'), so no local-time conversion is needed; the original CIC CSVs use local time. Sources: https://github.com/GintsEngelen/CNS2022_Code/blob/master/Labelling/CICIDS2017_labelling_fixed_CICFlowMeter.ipynb ; https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/CNS2022/Tools_Documentation.html

The attack time frames on the original CICIDS2017 web page are not accurate and do not allow exact reproduction of the original labelling; the WTMC2021 authors manually tuned windows (table on the page) and the CNS2022 notebook replaces them with first/last-packet UTC timestamps. Source: https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/WTMC2021/extended_doc.html

PCAP pre-processing: run pcapfix then reordercap on the original PCAPs before CICFlowMeter; in FTP-Patator a handful of flows looked victim-initiated because the SYN/ACK carried an earlier timestamp than the SYN (simulation environment issue), rectified by this step. Sources: https://github.com/GintsEngelen/CNS2022_Code/blob/master/README.md ; https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/CNS2022/CICIDS2017.html#2017_FTP_Patator

FTP-Patator: the very first attacker flow (src port 52108) is a successful login pre-test, labelled Attempted category 2; flows with a single failed login after a 5-minute idle are still labelled malicious. Source: https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/CNS2022/CICIDS2017.html#2017_FTP_Patator

SSH-Patator: one flow (src port 52056, 18:07:48 to 19:04:19 UTC, >1 hour, 1006-byte packet from port 22) is of uncertain legitimacy because the contents are encrypted; small-forward-payload TLS-handshake flows without login attempts are Attempted category 3; some flows are only the last 2 packets of a previous flow split by the 120 s flow timeout. Source: https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/CNS2022/CICIDS2017.html#2017_SSH_Patator

DoS Hulk is misimplemented: the Python tool's urllib2 sends 'Connection: close' instead of Keep-Alive, so the server closes every connection and the attack is almost completely ineffective; strictly all of it is Attempted category 5 but the authors keep the DoS Hulk label because the traffic still looks anomalous, and the WTMC2021 page recommends not using it as a malicious class. Sources: https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/CNS2022/CICIDS2017.html#2017_DoS_Hulk ; https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/WTMC2021/extended_doc.html

DoS Hulk: nearly the whole attack can be filtered with four Total Length of Bwd Packets values (11595, 23190, 11606, 23201); only 8 of 545,438 flows fall outside, and src ports 48678 and 43664 look like manual web browsing by the authors mid-attack (Attempted category 4). Source: https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/CNS2022/CICIDS2017.html#2017_DoS_Hulk

DoS GoldenEye is not very effective (some flows with Total Length of Bwd Packet = 0 show the server struggling); the Apache KeepAliveTimeout of 5 s shortens its connections and creates a shortcut-learning risk. Sources: https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/CNS2022/CICIDS2017.html#2017_Dos_GoldenEye ; https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/WTMC2021/extended_doc.html

DoS Slowloris: an accidental early launch between 2017-07-05 12:48:46.211817 and 12:48:46.264300 UTC is labelled Attempted category 5; the victim connection pool is exhausted around 12:49:12 (first unresponsive port 54470); src ports 33358/33360/33362 are tool-shutdown navigation (category 2) and 54114 is normal browsing (category 4); many connection attempts the server cannot answer are category 6. Source: https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/CNS2022/CICIDS2017.html#2017_DoS_Slowloris

DoS Slowloris documentation inconsistency: the authors' page prints the human-readable end '2017-07-05 14:20:08.91578' next to unix 1499260278.500956 (which is 13:11:18.500956 UTC); the notebook uses the unix value. Source: https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/CNS2022/CICIDS2017.html#2017_DoS_Slowloris

DoS Slowhttptest: src port 33372 is pre-attack navigation (category 2), src port 37670 is mid-attack navigation (category 4), and zero-payload retransmission flows with Flow Duration >= 199984 us and no backward packets are category 6; long Total TCP Flow Times show the attack worked. Source: https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/CNS2022/CICIDS2017.html#2017_DoS_Slowhttptest

Heartbleed: the original labelling is fine; the attack is a single src/dst port pair (45022 -> 444) with very long TCP duration, and the WTMC2021 regenerated dataset contains only 11 Heartbleed flows (0 Attempted) because the 120 s flow timeout splits the single connection. Sources: https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/CNS2022/CICIDS2017.html#2017_Heartbleed ; https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/WTMC2021/tools_datasets.html

Web Attack - SQL Injection: the first malicious packet occurs about 5 minutes earlier than the CIC time frame; set-up flows (src ports 36180-36188, 13:35:27.852814-13:35:45.720612 UTC) are Attempted category 2 and the src-port filter resolves a ~1 s overlap with XSS traffic; only 12 effective flows remain (WTMC count). Sources: https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/CNS2022/CICIDS2017.html#2017_Web_SQL ; https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/WTMC2021/tools_datasets.html

Web Attack - SQL Injection documentation inconsistency: the notebook applies the category-0 (no payload) rule to the set-up window without a port filter, whereas the authors' page lists it for the main window with 'Src Port not in [36180..36188]'. Sources: https://github.com/GintsEngelen/CNS2022_Code/blob/master/Labelling/CICIDS2017_labelling_fixed_CICFlowMeter.ipynb ; https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/CNS2022/CICIDS2017.html#2017_Web_SQL

Web Attack - XSS: the original labelling included startup/teardown traffic without malicious content; a Total Fwd Packets >= 150 threshold and the SQL-injection src-port exclusion isolate 27 effective flows versus 652 Attempted (WTMC counts). Sources: https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/CNS2022/CICIDS2017.html#2017_Web_XSS ; https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/WTMC2021/tools_datasets.html

Web Attack - Brute Force: the authors attacked the DVWA initial login page rather than the dedicated Brute Force page; the original logic yields 151 flows in two clusters (5 packets total: 72 flows; 204 fwd/105 bwd: 69 flows) and interlaced plain GET flows carry no attempt (Attempted category 4); WTMC counts 151 effective vs 1214 Attempted. Sources: https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/CNS2022/CICIDS2017.html#2017_Web_Brute_Force ; https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/WTMC2021/tools_datasets.html

Infiltration: the Dropbox download that delivered the (Meterpreter) payload to 192.168.10.8 cannot be identified among encrypted Dropbox connections (162.125.4.6, 162.125.4.5, 162.125.3.1, 162.125.248.1), so that traffic stays Benign; 192.168.10.9 made earlier connection attempts and Dropbox visits (possible dry run) labelled Attempted category 2. Source: https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/CNS2022/CICIDS2017.html#2017_Infiltration

Infiltration 'Cool disk - MAC' (192.168.10.25 <-> 205.174.165.73, victim port 51325, attacker port 444) was completely missed in the original labelling and is labelled on the basis of the Python Meterpreter push; the authors' page text contains the typos '205.174.165.74' and '102.168.10.25'. Source: https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/CNS2022/CICIDS2017.html#2017_Infiltration_Cooldisk

Thursday NMAP portscan: the official window is 18:04-18:45 UTC, but a round at 17:33 UTC (192.168.10.8 -> 192.168.10.5) is benign in the original dataset and absent from the CIC documentation; six scripted rounds (aa.bat) stop on 192.168.10.9 in the sixth; benign background 192.168.10.8 -> 192.168.10.50 flows are removed with packet-attribute filters (Fwd Packet Length Max 408, fwd payload 176 or 20514). Source: https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/CNS2022/CICIDS2017.html#2017_Infiltration_NMAP_Portscan

Friday portscan: the attacker also talks to IPs not listed as victims; the first round ran with the firewall on so only ports 21, 22, 80, 443 and 444 got through; start-up traffic is cut by the timestamps. Source: https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/CNS2022/CICIDS2017.html#2017_Infiltration_NMAP_Portscan

Botnet Ares: CnC connection attempts continue after the master is shut down and are Attempted category 1; the notebook starts that window at 14:03:00.000000 UTC while the page prints 14:03:14.356593. Sources: https://github.com/GintsEngelen/CNS2022_Code/blob/master/Labelling/CICIDS2017_labelling_fixed_CICFlowMeter.ipynb ; https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/CNS2022/CICIDS2017.html#2017_Botnet

DDoS LOIC HTTP (named 'LOIT' by CIC): mostly empty GET requests; identical packets and flows also occur outside the attack window as programmatically generated background (2-3 flows every 5-12 s), and the server kept responding for the whole attack. Source: https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/CNS2022/CICIDS2017.html#2017_DDoS_LOIC_HTTP

Notebook post-processing: rows containing 'Infinity' or NaN are dropped and flows with Flow ID '8.0.6.4-8.6.0.1-0-0-0' are forced to BENIGN as artefacts. Source: https://github.com/GintsEngelen/CNS2022_Code/blob/master/Labelling/CICIDS2017_labelling_fixed_CICFlowMeter.ipynb

Original CICFlowMeter flow construction: a flow ended at the first FIN and RST was ignored, and a timed-out flow's successor inherits its direction (TCP-appendix problem), which made attacker-initiated flows look victim-initiated and benign; the fixed tool terminates on mutual FIN or RST and the WTMC authors reconstructed or relabelled more than 20 percent of the original traces. Sources: https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/WTMC2021/extended_doc.html ; https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/WTMC2021/tools_datasets.html

Original CICIDS2017 feature bugs: TCP flag counts are only 0 or 1 (counted on the first packet only, fixed upstream 2019-10-15), Fwd/Bwd PSH and URG flags were not incremented, and Fwd Header Length is duplicated. Source: https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/WTMC2021/extended_doc.html

Apache Timeout/KeepAlive configuration of the victim web server is undocumented by CIC and creates inter-arrival-time shortcuts for Slowloris/Slowhttptest/GoldenEye. Source: https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/WTMC2021/extended_doc.html

WTMC2021 paper table error: the correct total of Attempted labels is 9103 and the correct Benign count for Intermediate and Final versions is 1657069. Source: https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/WTMC2021/tools_datasets.html

TCP segmentation offload: the authors' tools page only states 'Fixed TCP Segmentation Offset issue (more details in our paper under section IV-B)'; the CNS2022 paper is not openly available and no 2017-specific detail is given on the public pages, so nothing further could be transcribed. Source: https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/CNS2022/Tools_Documentation.html

'Attempted' flows must never be a separate class for a machine-learning model; when in doubt relabel them Benign (Attempted Category != -1). Source: https://intrusion-detection.distrinet-research.be/CNS2022/Dataset_Download.html

matcher_extensions_implemented.note: exclude_attack_payload_max_eq compares the attacker-side maximum TCP/UDP payload length of one packet (CICFlowMeter Fwd Packet Length Max); exclude_attack_payload_total_in compares the attacker-side total payload bytes. Fields inside any_of alternatives are evaluated by the EXP93 base matcher and do not see these extensions.
